sections.heading: More exploration, faster
sections.content: Belsky says strong product leaders already make time to explore many possibilities, narrow them down, get feedback, and refine a small set—often presenting two or three options. AI can expand the range they explore in far less time. For example, a Hollywood director asks ChatGPT for five scenarios while developing an idea; he doesn’t use those scenarios directly, but they surface possibilities, including approaches he would reject. The benefit is broader exploration, not handing over the decision.

sections.heading: Less handoff, more cross-functional work
sections.content: He also expects organizations to “collapse the stack”: people can get answers from data and pursue questions themselves instead of routing every request through specialists. That could enable more cross-functional work and give specialists, such as data analysts, more time for other thinking rather than repetitive requests. More broadly, Belsky sees AI reducing mundane workflow friction and helping people move from workflow to flow, with more room for human ingenuity.
